:::{#exm-quadratic-program}
#### The closest point of a half-plane to the origin

Minimizing $x_1^2 + x_2^2$ subject to $x_1 + x_2 \ge 1$
is a [quadratic program](#def-quadratic-program):
the [objective](#def-objective-function) is $\tfrac{1}{2}\,\qform{\matr{S}}{\vx}$ with $\matr{S} = 2 \matr{I}_2$,
which is [positive semidefinite](linear-algebra-special-matrices.qmd#def-positive-semidefinite);
$\vecf{c} = \vzero$;
and the single constraint is a linear [inequality](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/proof-writing.html#def-inequality).
The point $\tp{(0.5, 0.5)}$ is feasible,
since $0.5 + 0.5 = 1$,
and its objective value is

$$
\ba
f(0.5, 0.5)
&= 0.25 + 0.25
\\
&= 0.5.
\ea
$$

@fig-quadratic-program shows that it is the [minimizer](#def-minimizer-over-feasible-set):
it is where the smallest contour circle of the objective touches the feasible [half-plane](optimization-convexity.qmd#def-half-space).

:::{#fig-quadratic-program}

```{r}
#| label: quadratic-program-plot
#| code-fold: true
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Contour circles of x1 squared plus x2 squared around the origin, at
#|   heights 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2, drawn on equal axes. The shaded region above
#|   the line x1 + x2 = 1 is the feasible half-plane. A dot at (0.5, 0.5)
#|   marks where the circle at height 0.5 touches the line.
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-width: 4.5
# The objective on a grid, for its contour circles.
axis_values <- seq(-1.5, 1.5, length.out = 301)
grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(x1 = axis_values, x2 = axis_values)
grid <- dplyr::mutate(grid, f = x1^2 + x2^2)

# The feasible half-plane x1 + x2 >= 1, clipped to the plotted square.
feasible <- tibble::tribble(
  ~x1, ~x2,
  -0.5, 1.5,
  1.5, 1.5,
  1.5, -0.5
)
# Contour heights: 0.5 is the minimum over the half-plane; the others frame it.
heights <- c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2)
limits <- c(-1.5, 1.5)
minimizer <- tibble::tibble(x1 = 0.5, x2 = 0.5)

grid |>
  ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::aes(x = x1, y = x2) +
  ggplot2::geom_polygon(data = feasible, fill = "grey85") +
  ggplot2::geom_abline(intercept = 1, slope = -1) +
  ggplot2::geom_contour(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(z = f),
    breaks = heights, # check-unexplained-choices: allow
    colour = "grey30"
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = minimizer, size = 3) +
  ggplot2::coord_fixed(xlim = limits, ylim = limits) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "first coordinate", y = "second coordinate")
```

The [objective](#def-objective-function) $x_1^2 + x_2^2$ has circular contours at heights $0.25$, $0.5$, $1$ and $2$.
The shaded [half-plane](optimization-convexity.qmd#def-half-space) satisfies $x_1 + x_2 \ge 1$,
and the dot at $(0.5, 0.5)$ is where the contour at height $0.5$ touches its edge.
:::

@fig-quadratic-program-3d shows the same [function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-function) as a surface.
